what_its_for: Betaxolol is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) when taken as a tablet. It is also available as eye drops to treat a type of glaucoma (high pressure in the eye) called open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension. It works by blocking certain signals in your heart and blood vessels to lower blood pressure, or in your eye to reduce fluid buildup.
how_to_take: For tablets: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. For eye drops: Wash your hands before use. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to make a small pocket, and place one drop inside. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes and press lightly on the inner corner of your eye to keep the medicine from draining away. Do not touch the dropper tip to your eye or any other surface to avoid contamination. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between each medication.
dosing: For high blood pressure (tablets): The usual starting dose is 10 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to 20 mg once daily if needed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. For glaucoma (eye drops): The usual dose is 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye(s) twice daily. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store betaxolol tablets and eye drops at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the medication away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use eye drops if the liquid looks cloudy or discolored, or if particles are visible.
what_to_avoid: Avoid stopping this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause serious problems such as chest pain or worsening heart conditions. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it may lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness. Be careful when driving, operating machinery, or doing activities that require alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting out of bed or standing up too quickly, as this medication can cause dizziness, especially when you first start taking it.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: slow or irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath or wheezing, sudden weight gain or swelling in your legs or feet, severe dizziness or fainting, cold or numb hands and feet, unusual tiredness or weakness, signs of depression such as mood changes or sleep problems, or any new or worsening symptoms. For eye drops, call your doctor if you notice eye redness, pain, swelling, discharge, or worsening vision after use.
when_it_works: For high blood pressure: You may start to notice an effect within a few hours after your first dose, but it may take 1 to 2 weeks of regular use to see the full benefit. For glaucoma eye drops: The medication begins to lower eye pressure within about 30 minutes of each dose, with the maximum effect occurring within about 2 hours. Continue using this medication even if you feel well, as high blood pressure and glaucoma often have no symptoms.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to the side effects of betaxolol, especially dizziness and slow heart rate. Use caution when standing up to prevent falls. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have kidney or liver disease. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medication. Children: The safety and effectiveness of betaxolol tablets in children have not been well established. Consult your doctor. People with asthma or breathing problems: Although betaxolol is considered a selective beta-blocker and may be safer than some others, it can still sometimes worsen breathing problems. Always tell your doctor about any breathing conditions you have before starting this medication. Diabetes: Betaxolol may hide some signs of low blood sugar such as a fast heartbeat. Monitor your blood sugar closely and talk to your doctor.
